sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's renewable build-out is accelerating on government-mandated captive power plant quotas, giving BATR and POWR durable volume growth independent of global rate cycles.
US utility outperformance is structurally tied to AI/data-center load growth, favoring vertically integrated players (DUK, AEE, XEL) with regulated recovery mechanisms over merchant-exposed names.
Climate-tech capital costs remain elevated, but falling solar module and battery prices are improving project IRRs, supporting selective long positions in developers with contracted offtake.
sectors.ai: Buy BATR and POWR on relative strength within a flat sector; both are outperforming on Indonesia-specific catalysts (capacity additions, tariff clarity). Trim EIX/PCG exposure as US utility gains look rate-driven and mean-reverting. Maintain neutral aggregate weight, but rotate into ID names with earnings momentum and away from US regulated utilities until the Fed signals a definitive cut.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Indonesia's consumer staples demand is structurally supported by a young, urbanizing population and rising middle-class spending on protein and packaged foods.
Small-cap FMCG names are benefiting from domestic distribution expansion into tier-2/3 cities, where local brands are gaining share against multinationals.
Regulatory stability and government food-security programs create a durable tailwind for meat, dairy, and agro-processing sub-sectors.
sectors.ai: Buy selective small-cap FMCG names with confirmed volume spikes (PADA, JARR, PGUN) as momentum is broad-based and signal remains NORMAL, but avoid chasing BEEF/AGAR after >12% single-day runs. Rotate into SMGA and SIPD for relative-value upside; trim any exposure to laggards as the tape favors high-beta names.
